question.text: Money laundering under PMLA 2002 is defined as the process of disguising the proceeds of crime as legitimate income. Which of the following is NOT an element of the offense of money laundering under the Act?

answer.text: Directly or indirectly attempting to indulge in concealment of proceeds of crime
Possession or acquisition of proceeds of crime
Failing to file income tax returns on proceeds of crime within the due date
Projecting or claiming proceeds of crime as untainted property

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook lists the elements of the PMLA offence as concealment, possession, acquisition, use, projecting as untainted property, and claiming as untainted property of proceeds of crime. Failure to file income-tax returns is not one of these listed PMLA elements. The Trap: Candidates may treat non-filing of tax returns on illegal proceeds as automatically falling within PMLA. On the checked source page, PMLA is restricted to the listed elements above; tax-return non-filing is outside that list. Note: Source basis is p.355 of the NISM-Series-X-A Investment Adviser (Level 1) workbook (June 2025).
